text:
Maria: heads-up, ran a night profiler against main after the rolling deploy — P99 token latency spiked ~2.5x on mid-size models. suspicious pattern around cache churn and batch composition.

Kevin: ugh. repro steps?

Maria: quick notes: workload is steady stream of short prompts + occasional long generations. saw big prefill batches absorbing most of the KV warmups, then decode batches arriving with cold KV -> cache thrash. attached flame snapshot (short).

Chia: can you paste the flame snippet?

Maria: here's the key stack we saw: 
```
GPU memcpy -> KV populate -> kernel_select::fallback_path -> long-nop
batcher::form_batch (size 48) -> prefill_path -> KV evict
```
Not super pretty. Looks like big mixed-phase batches are forcing kernels to choose generic slow paths.

Kevin: hmm mixing prefill+decode in same batch means kernel selector can't pick the optimized decode kernels. we should try separating the queues so kernel_affinity stays consistent.

Sam: proposal: split the incoming queue into two fast lanes: warmup (prefill) and generation (decode). enforce token_budget per-lane: prefill_budget=64, decode_budget=12. That should keep persistent KV live for decode-heavy lanes.

Chia: +1. also add a soft affinity tag on the request object so kernel_selector can prefer instruction-friendly kernels for decode. cheap to add.

Maria: quick config I tested locally that improved things a lot: 
```yaml
batching:
  split_phase_queues: true
  prefill_token_budget: 64
  decode_token_budget: 12
  max_batch_size: 64
  per_queue_kernel_affinity:
    prefill: "kernels:fp16_wide"
    decode: "kernels:fp16_stream"
  kv_priming_window_ms: 50
```
Ran bench with `./bench --mode=split --rps=300 --model=redwood-tiny`

Kevin: numbers?

Maria: baseline (combined batching): p50=22ms p95=180ms p99=420ms. with split lanes + kernel affinity: p50=20ms p95=110ms p99=160ms. CPU/GPU profiles show KV fill ops down ~3x at hot paths.

Sam: wow p99 improvement is solid. did you test throughput impact?

Maria: throughput flat (within 3%), slight increase in token/sec since fewer kernel fallbacks. cost per-token slightly down.

Chia: couple cautions: 1) some tiny prompts end up starved if decode_budget too low -> they get funneled into prefill lane and wait. 2) KV memory footprint increased slightly due to priming window retaining warmed segments.

Kevin: we can mitigate (1) with a tiny fast-path for sub-8-token requests that short-circuit to decode lane if latency-sensitive. for (2) add a cap on primed_kv_bytes and a fast-evict policy if memory > threshold.

Maria: wrote a quick experiment PR (link: https://git.redwood/repo/pull/1245) that wires split queues + kernel affinity + priming window. test bench job is attached to PR.

perf-bot: benchmark job #1245 completed — p99 improved 160ms vs baseline 420ms, diff -62%.

Sam: ok next steps: 1) run canary on dedicated pool C (low-traffic) for 2h with observability flags: token_latency, kv_hit_rate, kernel_fallback_rate. 2) if stable, increase to 50% traffic and run 24h.

Kevin: add a metric: batch_phase_entropy — high entropy = bad (mixed phases). trigger alert when >0.3 for >5m.

Maria: added to dashboard: /dash/eng-runtime/batches -> shows phase entropy, p95, p99, kv_evictions/s.

deploy-bot: starting canary deploy to pool-c tag=canary-split-queues (sha=de12f3a)

Chia: FYI I ran a quick kernel affinity microbench — decode-optimized kernel is ~1.8x faster on 1-16 token decode scenarios, prefill kernel better for long prefills. matches our hypothesis.

Sam: sounds good. let's watch memory + tiny-prompt latency during canary. assign follow-ups: @Kevin -> alert + dashboard tweaks; @Maria -> collect canary traces and attach to PR; @Chia -> add fast-exit for sub-8 tokens.

Kevin: on it.

Maria: thanks team. will post canary updates in this thread. :thumbsup:
